title: Backlog Document v1
description: The single-source specs/backlog/BACKLOG.json document (operator ruling 2026-08-28: 'BACKLOG.md e BACKLOG.json — estruturado' — the live-photo Markdown grammar, ## ACTIVE with ### <slug> subsections plus fenced-YAML **Intents:** blocks, is retired; every field it carried becomes a native JSON field, nothing lost). One document, one top-level object: 'active' is the live photo of every candidate/idea backlog item (mirrors the retired ActiveItem shape 1:1 — id/title/opened/status/description/provenance plus an optional typed intents[] array, no more fenced YAML). A closed item's terminal record does NOT live in this document — it already moved to the append-only, JSON-native specs/backlog/_archive/backlog_histo.jsonl at v0.5.0 FR5 (one BacklogHistoRecord line per exit), and stays there: folding a mutable live list and an immutable append-only exit ledger back into one rewritten-in-place JSON blob would resurrect the exact duplicate-closure failure mode (the retired in-document ## LEDGER, BL-DUP) that FR5 deleted structurally, not merely disabled. 'schema' pins the document version so a reader never has to sniff a Markdown-vs-JSON ambiguity again.

schema.description: Document schema id — always the literal string 'backlog-v1'.

active.description: One entry per live candidate/idea backlog item, in document order — the exact set the retired '## ACTIVE' Markdown section held, one '### <slug>' subsection per array entry. 'id' is unique within this array (the retired same-slug-twice-in-ACTIVE check, now a plain array-uniqueness invariant enforced by dadaia_workspace.features.backlog.document.load_document, surfaced as BL-SCHEMA — BL-DUP itself stays deleted, not reinstated, per v0.5.0 A5.2: a duplicate EXIT is still structurally impossible because exits never land back in this array).

id.description: Backlog slug — the retired '### <slug>' heading text. Stable identity; never renumbered or reused.

title.description: Short human-readable name — the retired '**Title:**' bullet.

opened.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the entry was opened — the retired '**Opened:**' bullet.

status.description: Live-stage token (e.g. 'idea', 'candidate', 'picked', or another live/non-terminal token) — the retired '**Status:**' bullet. The backlog status vocabulary is deliberately informal beyond the 'idea' intents-exemption gate (dd-backlog-definition SS2); the six canonical TERMINAL disposition tokens (core.models.backlog.TERMINAL_DISPOSITION_TOKENS) are refused here by BL-STALE — a terminal status belongs to a backlog_histo.jsonl record, never a live 'active' entry.

description.description: One-paragraph description of the need — the retired '**Description:**' bullet.

provenance.description: Where this entry came from (operator request, or an intake-report item id + approval date) — the retired '**Provenance:**' bullet.

intents.description: Optional typed intents[] — the retired fenced ```yaml **Intents:** code span, now native JSON. Every subject binds one change to one canonical subject anchor (dadaia_workspace.core.models.backlog.parse_intents is the one parser/validator, shared by both the pre-migration Markdown reader's old fenced block and this native array). Required once 'status' matures past 'idea' (dd-backlog-definition SS2, BL-SCHEMA); absent or empty is doctor-clean at 'idea'.

kind.description: The registry source class this subject ref resolves against (dadaia_workspace.core.models.backlog.SubjectKind).

ref.description: The typed reference itself — 'path/to/module.py#Symbol' for kind=code (module-relative only; an absolute/operator-local path is refused at construction), a 'dadaia <command>' id for kind=cli, a catalog.json feature slug for kind=catalog, a SPEC-DOC id or memory heading anchor for kind=doc, an INV-* id for kind=invariant.

surface.description: 'existing' (default) — ref must resolve to a live registry anchor. 'new' — this item INTRODUCES the surface; bound by declared identity, never forced onto an unrelated existing anchor.

change.description: Human-readable delta this item proposes for the bound subject.
